rows.name: LOWESTOFT
rows.character: Upper rev. br. lt., ½ min. Lower occulting red or bright light, ½ min. (High light to North)
rows.description: White lt.-houses, 53 and 48 ft. high, 830 yards apart, S.S.E. and N.N.W. High lt. on cliff, low lt. on ness. Low lt., eclipsed for 3 secs. every ½ min., is red over line of sands from N.N.E., seaward, to S.W. by S., and bright over in-shore channels. High lt.-ho. shows lower fixed red lt., betw. N.E. and N.E. by N., as a guide to round the ness. (The red lt. on N. pier is masked in-shore of N.E. by E. ½ E. for same purpose.) When red lt. from high tower opens from the northward, haul into red lt. from low lt.-ho. until N. pier red lt. opens, when run for it until low red lt. changes to bright

rows.name: Lowestoft Harbour
rows.description: Red lts. on pier-heads. Two green lts. at entr. of inner harb. Red lt. at fish-market when 10 ft. water, green when less. Green lt. at end of North pier works

rows.name: Corton Lightvessel
rows.description: Fairway light in 12½ fms., outside Corton Sand. Red, with half ball below usual ball

rows.name: St. Nicholas Gat Lt.-Ves.
rows.character: One fixed bright light One flash. red lt., 10 secs.
rows.description: In 10 fathoms, at inner end of channel. Red, with ball. Red light on mizen-mast

rows.name: Yarmouth, or Gorleston
rows.character: 1. One fixed Tide light 2. Two fixed red lights
rows.description: 1. On South pier. Light is red with flood tide (red flag by day), but green with ebb 2. In line, S.W. ½ S., clear Caistor Shoal; one on Sailor's Home, one on Britannia Pier A fixed green light on Britannia Pier-head

rows.name: MIDDLE CROSS SAND LIGHTVESSEL
rows.description: Painted red, with two broad vertical black stripes; two cones, points together, at the mast-head. In 19¾ fathoms, nearly 7 miles S. by W., westerly, from Newarp lightvessel. A 5-secs. flash followed by a short flash, then eclipsed 17½ secs. Explosive Rockets fired when a vessel is in dangerous proximity

rows.name: Cockle Lightvessel
rows.description: In 7 fathoms, at East side of North entrance of Cockle Gat. Red, with ball

rows.name: WINTERTON NESS
rows.description: A circular red tower, 69 ft. high. Lt. masked to S. by E. ½ E. to Scroby Elbow bell buoy

rows.name: NEWARP LT.-VESSEL
rows.description: In 17 fathoms, North end of sand, with three masts and balls. Light gives 3 quick flashes, then eclipsed 36 secs.

rows.name: WOULD LIGHTVESSEL
rows.description: In 15 fms., off South end of Hasborough Sand, 6 miles N. by W. ½ W. from Newarp lightvessel. Red, with diamond at mast-head

rows.name: HASBOROUGH
rows.character: One occult. br. lt., ½ m.
rows.description: White tower, 85 feet high, S.S.E. of church. Lt. eclipsed for 5 secs. once in every ½ min.

rows.name: HASBOROUGH LT.-VES.
rows.description: In 14 fathoms, near North end of sand, 10 miles E. ½ S. from Cromer lighthouse; lights horizontal. Red, with two red balls

rows.name: SMITH'S KNOLL LT.-V.
rows.character: One 2-flash. red and br. light, 20 secs.
rows.description: Red, with black bulwarks, and a black ball at mast-head. Moored in 25½ fms., 1 mile E. of the shoal, and 17½ miles S. ¾ E. from Leman and Ower lightvessel. Light shows a red and a bright flash, followed by 12 secs. eclipse

rows.name: LEMAN & OWER LT.-V.
rows.description: In 16 fathoms between the Sands. Light shows 2 quick flashes, followed by 20 secs. darkness. Red, two masts and balls

rows.name: CROMER
rows.description: White tower, 58 ft. high, near the cliff

rows.name: HUNSTANTON
rows.character: One occult. br. lt., ½ m.
rows.description: White tower, 61 ft. high, on the point. Two quick occultations, followed by 24 secs. light. Red over Roaring Middle Sand, between W. by N. ¾ N. and N.W. by W. ½ W.

rows.name: Lynn Well Lightvessel
rows.description: In 17½ fathoms, off the hook of the Long Sand. Red, with ball at mast-head

rows.name: Lynn Channel Lt.-Vessel
rows.description: Moored in 3½ fms., at N.E. end of Wisbeach Bar Flat, 8 miles above Lynn Well lt.-vessel

rows.name: Lynn
rows.description: Leading lights on East side of entrance to cut; in one, S. ¾ E., 555 ft. apart

rows.name: Boston
rows.description: Two fixed bright leading lights at Hob Hole

rows.name: Skegness
rows.description: Two fixed bright lights, vertical, at end of pier

rows.name: Inner Dowsing Lt.-Ves.
rows.description: In 10 fathoms, near N.E. end of shoal. Red, with two balls vertically

rows.name: DUDGEON LT.-VESSEL
rows.description: In 10½ fathoms, 1 mile S.W. of shoalest part. Red, with ball at mast-head. Two quick flashes, first bright, second red, followed by an eclipse of 22 secs.
